THE OPERATING PROBLEM

A continuous feed needs a focused review queue.

A camera network produces long periods of footage. A supervisor needs the event, relevant time window and site rule together, without repeated alerts for the same occurrence.

01

A single event can generate many repeated frame detections.

Video is a continuous workload. The system checks frames for defined events, groups repeated detections and sends only the relevant time window for a supervisor to review.

02

The supervisor needs a timestamp and camera reference.

The useful output needs the original reference and a clear next action.

03

The site must control authorized monitoring and evidence retention.

No face identification or automatic emergency dispatch. A supervisor verifies every event and follows the site’s response procedure.

WHY NOW

Review the event instead of replaying the day.

Defined event models can support a bounded review task when they are evaluated against authorized footage. The useful product is a grouped time window that a supervisor can verify, with false and missed events measured.
